search_log: Searched "The Last Mile" "David Baldacci" excerpt, first chapter, official excerpt, and publisher-page combinations.

Searched "The Last Mile" with point of view, third person, narrator, narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view; no credible source explicitly describing a different or alternating person was found.
Opened the Hachette Book Group title page; it verified the work but supplied only synopsis-level prose.
Opened the Everand Spanish-edition preview; its sustained opening and continuation into Chapter 2 showed third-person narration centered on Melvin Mars.
Checked Google Books for the Pan Macmillan edition; the page reported that no preview was available.

Reviewed Kirkus, Publishers Weekly, Bookreporter, and Washington Independent reviews; they corroborated the characters and novel-wide focus but did not explicitly identify grammatical narrative person.
Exact-phrase searches for several Goodreads passages found the Goodreads quote page and non-authoritative reproductions; the latter were not used as evidence.

Independent audit reopened the Everand listing and verified that it identifies the Spanish ebook's publisher, ISBN, and subscription preview; the accessible prose reaches Chapter 3. The source remains Tier A as a commercial licensed ebook preview, but its opening-only scope does not support high confidence by itself.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and narrates Melvin Mars, Amos Decker, and other characters in third person, with access to their perceptions and thoughts. Multiple interior quotations agree with Everand's sustained, publisher-identified Spanish ebook preview through Chapter 3; apparent first- and second-person forms are dialogue, represented thought, or aphorism. THIRD is retained, but confidence is medium because the sole diagnostic web route is a translated opening and Hachette's English page provides only nondiagnostic synopsis. q01063 was reduced to unmarked because its isolated 'him/he' does not preserve an antecedent. Independent audit: verified Everand's commercial edition metadata and expanded opening coverage, retained Tier A, and calibrated confidence consistently with prior opening-only Baldacci cases.
